claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
The feedstock is suitable for additive manufacturing.
High-temperature build-platform preheating is the proposed intervention during additive manufacturing.
Build-platform preheating will reduce cooling rates.
Build-platform preheating will reduce thermal gradients at the build surface.
Reduced thermal gradients will produce more controlled solidification rates.
Preheating mitigates the thermal shock associated with rapid cooling.
A lower solidification rate reduces localized thermal stresses.
A lower solidification rate limits compositional segregation.
Reduced thermal stress and segregation lead to fewer defects.
Fewer defects and reduced segregation improve mechanical performance.
Preheated samples will have statistically significantly lower residual stress than samples produced without preheating.
Preheated samples will exhibit less microstructural segregation than samples produced without preheating.
Preheated samples will exhibit lower defect density than samples produced without preheating.
Preheated samples will exhibit enhanced tensile properties and hardness relative to samples produced without preheating.
AlCrFeNiSi parts made without platform preheating typically have higher residual stress, marked segregation, and increased defect density because of rapid cooling.
The effectiveness and optimum preheat temperature may be specific to AlCrFeNiSi composition and processing parameters.

contradictions.description: The comparator is not defined consistently. The hypothesis invokes 'conventional fabrication,' while the predicted outcome compares preheated and non-preheated additive manufacturing, and the baseline calls non-preheated builds 'conventionally fabricated.' Conventional bulk fabrication and additive manufacturing without platform preheating are not necessarily the same baseline.
